'''Frederic Tamler Sommers''' (January 1, 1923 &ndash; October 2, 2014), better known as '''Fred Sommers''', was an American philosopher who, after an initial focus on [[ontology]] generally, turned his attention specifically to a revival of [[classical logic]]. He is the father of the philosopher [[Tamler Sommers]].

==Birth and education==
Sommers was born in [[New York City]] on January 1, 1923.<ref name="DMAP">''The Dictionary Of Modern American Philosophers'', Thoemmes,  2005, p. 2281.</ref> His family was Jewish and he studied under Rabbi Joseph Soloveitchik in the 1950s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/belief/articles/covid-haredi-magical-thinking |title=COVID-19, Haredi Jewry, and 'Magical' Thinking |work=Tabletmag.com |date=April 5, 2020 |accessdate=April 30, 2020}}</ref> He received his BA and PhD in philosophy at [[Columbia University]], his dissertation being entitled ''An Empiricist Ontology: A Study in the Metaphysics of [[Alfred North Whitehead]].''<ref name="DMAP" />

==Career==
Sommers began his academic career at [[Columbia University]],<ref>''The Old New Logic: Essays on the Philosophy of Fred Sommers'', MIT Press 2005, p. 1.</ref> where he was assistant professor of philosophy from 1955 to 1963. He was invited to [[Brandeis University]] in 1964 as an associate professor of philosophy and was promoted to full professor in 1966.<ref name="DMAP" />  From 1965 until his retirement, he held the [[Harry Austryn Wolfson]] Chair of Philosophy; from 1993 until his death he was professor emeritus of Philosophy at Brandeis. He died aged 91 in 2014.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141006083605/http://leiterreports.typepad.com/blog/2014/10/in-memoriam-fred-sommers-1923-2014.html In Memoriam: Fred Sommers (1923-2014)]</ref>

==Bibliography==
*''An Empiricist Ontology. A Study in the Metaphysics of Alfred North Whitehead'', Columbia University, 1955 (unpublished Ph.D. thesis)
*''The Logic of Natural Language'', Oxford University Press, 1984. {{ISBN|978-0198247401}}
*''An Invitation to Formal Reasoning'', with George Englebretsen and Harry A. Wolfson. Ashgate, 2000. {{ISBN|978-0754613664}}
*''Vice and Virtue in Everyday Life: Introductory Readings in Ethics'', with [[Christina Hoff Sommers]]. Harcourt Brace, 1989. 9th edition: {{ISBN|978-1111837549}}
